1.title: Deploying with CI/CD, IaC and Containers
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Deploying with C I or C D, I A C and Containers. It covers the exam area Domain three: Testing and Deployment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Use Lambda deployment packaging methods (three point three.one). Deploy containerized applications with E C S, E K S and Fargate (three point three.two). Use infrastructure as code templates (three point three.three). Deploy revisions with Code Deploy (three point three.four). Orchestrate pipelines with Code Pipeline (three point three.five). Implement deployment strategies (three point three.six). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain three: Testing and Deployment (twenty-two percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: The CI/CD services
1.text: The C I or C D services. The figure shows this: Code Pipeline stages: source, build with Code Build, test, approval, deploy with Code Deploy or Cloud Formation.

1.title: The CI/CD services, continued
1.text: The C I or C D services. A W S Code Pipeline. Orchestrates the stages: source, build, test, approval, deploy. A W S Code Build. Builds and tests code in managed containers; defined by buildspec dot yml. A W S Code Deploy. Deploys revisions to E C two, on-premises servers, Lambda and E C S; defined by appspec. A W S Code Artifact. Package repository for dependencies. buildspec dot yml phases: install, pre build, build, post build, plus artifacts and cache. Code Pipeline passes artifacts between stages through S three, and can include a manual approval action.

1.title: CodeDeploy
1.text: Code Deploy. E C two or on-premises. In-place (stop, install, start) or blue or green; App Spec hooks: Before Install, After Install, Application Start, Validate Service. Lambda. Shifts traffic between versions with an alias: canary, linear or all at once. E C S. Blue or green with a load balancer shifting traffic to a new task set. Automatic rollback can be triggered by failed deployment or a Cloud Watch alarm. Exam tip: Gradual Lambda release with automatic rollback equals Code Deploy with an alias and a canary or linear configuration plus alarms.

1.title: Deployment strategies
1.text: Deployment strategies. All at once. Behavior: Replace everything now. Risk: Downtime, fast, hard rollback. Rolling. Behavior: Update batches. Risk: Reduced capacity during the update. Rolling with additional batch. Behavior: Add new capacity first. Risk: Keeps full capacity, costs more. Immutable. Behavior: Launch new instances, swap. Risk: Safe, easy rollback, uses more capacity.

1.title: Deployment strategies, continued
1.text: Deployment strategies. Blue or green. Behavior: Two environments, switch traffic. Risk: Fast cutover and rollback, double cost during the switch. Canary. Behavior: Small share of users first. Risk: Limits blast radius. Linear. Behavior: Shift traffic in equal steps. Risk: Predictable, slower.

1.title: Infrastructure as code
1.text: Infrastructure as code. A W S Cloud Formation. Jason or Y A M L templates that create stacks; change sets preview changes; automatic rollback on failure; drift detection. A W S S A M. Extension of Cloud Formation for serverless: a short A W S Serverless syntax, sam build, sam deploy. A W S C D K. Define infrastructure in a programming language; synthesizes Cloud Formation. Exam tip: "Preview what a template update will change" equals change set. Stack creation failure rolls back by default.

1.title: Containers and source control
1.text: Containers and source control. Amazon E C S. Run containers from a task definition; Fargate (no servers) or E C two launch type; services do rolling updates or blue or green. Amazon E K S. Managed Kubernetes; deploy manifests (Deployments, Services). Lambda packaging. .zip, container image, layers (Module eleven). Source control. Branches per environment or feature, tags and labels for releases, pull requests for review. A I in C I or C D. Automated approvals, environment provisioning and post-deployment validation can use A I tools; keep human approval for production. Exam tip: Code Pipeline orchestrates, Code Build builds, Code Deploy deploys. Know which verb belongs to which service.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants a pipeline that builds, tests and deploys on every commit. Which service orchestrates the stages? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A W S Code Pipeline. Code Pipeline orchestrates source, build, test and deploy stages.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which file tells Code Build what commands to run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: buildspec.yml. The buildspec defines Code Build's phases and artifacts.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A team releases a Lambda update to ten percent of traffic first and rolls back if an alarm fires. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Code Deploy canary deployment with an alias and an alarm. Code Deploy shifts alias traffic gradually with automatic rollback on alarms.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which strategy launches new instances and swaps them in, making rollback easy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Immutable. Immutable deployments use fresh instances and are easy to roll back.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team wants to see what a Cloud Formation update will change before applying it. What should they create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A change set. Change sets preview stack changes.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team wants serverless resources in a short template syntax. Which tool fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A W S S A M. S A M extends Cloud Formation for serverless.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. A containerized app should run without managing servers. Which E C S launch type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A W S Fargate. Fargate runs containers without managing instances.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which service orchestrates a C I or C D pipeline? Answer: A W S Code Pipeline. Question two. What are the buildspec phases? Answer: Install, pre build, build and post build. Question three. Name two Lambda traffic-shifting configurations. Answer: Canary and linear (or all at once).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a Cloud Formation change set? Answer: A preview of the changes an update would make. Question five. What does S A M stand for? Answer: Serverless Application Model. Question six. What does C D K do? Answer: Defines infrastructure in a programming language and synthesizes Cloud Formation.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. C I or C D: Code Pipeline orchestrates; Code Build (buildspec); Code Deploy (appspec); approvals. Strategies: all at once, rolling, rolling plus batch, immutable, blue or green, canary, linear. I A C: Cloud Formation (change sets, rollback, drift), S A M (serverless), C D K (code). Containers: E C S (task definition, Fargate), E K S (manifests). Rollback: Cloud Formation automatic; Code Deploy on failure or alarm.
